headline: KSE-100 rallies 1,647 points to 170,512 on Hormuz relief; oil jumps anew as Saudi pipeline stays shut and Iran-GCC talks are postponed into FOMC week
mood: Friday relief rally meets weekend oil shock · SBP and the Fed are this week's swing factors

snapshot.label: Brent / WTI
snapshot.delta: Sat pipeline shut · Mon talks postponed

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Snaps Back On Hormuz Hopes
five_things.html: The benchmark surged 1,646.81 points (0.98%) to close at 170,511.85 on Friday, recovering from an early slide to an intraday low of 166,141.17 after reports that Gulf states and Iran would meet in Oman to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Traded volume jumped to 687.47 million shares (Rs33.70 billion) from Thursday's 628.67 million (Rs27.02 billion), with 248 of 500 names advancing against 210 decliners and 42 unchanged; heavyweights Meezan Bank (MEBL), Fauji Fertilizer (FFC), Lucky Cement (LUCK), PPL and OGDC together added 1,032 points even as autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power lagged intraday. Cnergyico PK led volume with 104.27 million shares. Sources: Business Recorder, Trading Economics.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Rebounds As Core CPI Cools
five_things.html: US equities snapped a four-day losing streak Friday: the S&P 500 rose 0.9% (+65.28 pts) to 7,656.98, the Dow gained 1.0% (+509.19 pts) to 52,573.29 and the Nasdaq added 1.0% (+251.31 pts) to 26,333.04, as August headline CPI (+0.4% m/m, +3.4% y/y, unchanged from July) matched forecasts even as core inflation ticked up to +0.3% m/m. Fed funds futures still pushed the odds of a 25bp hike at next week's 15-16 September FOMC meeting to roughly 86-90%, up sharply from about 70-72% a day earlier. The 10-year Treasury yield eased slightly to 4.95% after nearing 5% mid-week, while the 2-year held near 4.63%. Sources: CNBC, Advisor Perspectives.
five_things.sentiment: relief rally, but hawkish Fed repricing intact

five_things.chip: Oil Jumps Anew On Pipeline Shutdown, Postponed Talks
five_things.html: Brent had eased 2.8% to $104.61/bbl and WTI 2.4% to $100.05 on Friday as hopes built for Oman-hosted talks between Iran and the GCC on reopening the Strait of Hormuz — but that relief unwound over the weekend. Saudi Arabia kept its 7m-bpd East-West pipeline shut after 10-11 September drone strikes damaged pump stations near Riyadh and Medina, removing the kingdom's main Hormuz bypass for roughly 5m bpd of rerouted crude, and Oman late Sunday postponed indefinitely the Monday summit in Salalah after Bahrain declined to attend. Oil gapped higher in early Monday trade on the news. Sources: CNBC, Al Jazeera.

five_things.chip: Gold, Silver Soft Into Fed Week
five_things.html: Gold held roughly flat at $4,385.61/oz (+0.06%) and silver fell 2.6% to $64.90/oz on Friday as investors weighed in-line headline CPI against surging Fed hike odds; early Monday trade saw spot gold slip a further 0.3-0.8% toward the $4,334-4,375 band as the oil-driven inflation shock reinforced the case for a hike. Both metals remain well inside their 2026 uptrend despite the pullback. Sources: USAGOLD, Yahoo Finance.
five_things.sentiment: consolidating, rate-hike odds capping the haven bid

five_things.chip: SBP Decision, IMF Mission In Focus
five_things.html: The State Bank's Monetary Policy Committee meets today, with markets broadly expecting the policy rate to hold at 11.5% for a fourth straight meeting, as August CPI at 11.15% y/y and a fresh oil-driven inflation risk limit room to ease; 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.87%. The government's Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue ahead of an IMF mission for the fourth EFF/third RSF review expected in Karachi and Islamabad in the coming weeks, widely flagged around 22-23 September. Sources: Business Recorder, Business Recorder.
five_things.sentiment: policy hold expected, IMF scrutiny ahead

matrix.local_html: The KSE-100 surged 1,646.81 points (0.98%) to close at 170,511.85 on Friday, clawing back roughly half of Thursday's 3,079-point rout after reports of a planned Iran-GCC meeting on the Strait of Hormuz lifted sentiment; volume jumped to 687.47 million shares (Rs33.70bn) with 248 of 500 names advancing. That relief now looks fragile: the State Bank's Monetary Policy Committee meets today and is widely expected to hold the policy rate at 11.5% given August CPI at 11.15% y/y and 6-month KIBOR near 11.87%, while USD/PKR interbank was broadly steady around 277.35-277.55. On policy, the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue ahead of the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review mission, expected in the coming weeks and widely flagged around 22-23 September. Sources: Business Recorder, Business Recorder.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf oil markets swung sharply into the weekend: Brent eased to $104.61/bbl and WTI to $100.05 on Friday as an Oman-hosted summit between Iran and the GCC on reopening the Strait of Hormuz raised de-escalation hopes, only for Oman to postpone the talks indefinitely late Sunday after Bahrain declined to attend. Compounding the supply risk, Saudi Arabia's 7m-bpd East-West pipeline — its main bypass for roughly 5m bpd of crude that would otherwise transit Hormuz — remains shut following 10-11 September drone strikes on pump stations near Riyadh and Medina, itself days after Houthi strikes wounded 73 and disrupted energy sites including the 400,000-bpd Jazan refinery. OPEC+'s seven core producers held October quotas unchanged near 31.01m bpd at their 6 September meeting. Away from the war premium, non-oil momentum held up: UAE and Saudi PMIs stood at 55.3 and 53.8 respectively in August, both multi-month highs. Sources: Bloomberg, Al Jazeera.
matrix.global_html: US equities snapped a four-day losing streak Friday as August CPI matched forecasts: the S&P 500 rose 0.9% to 7,656.98, the Dow gained 1.0% to 52,573.29 and the Nasdaq added 1.0% to 26,333.04. Even so, a firmer core reading pushed fed funds futures odds of a 25bp hike at next week's 15-16 September FOMC meeting to roughly 86-90%, up from about 70-72% a day earlier, as the 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.95% after nearing 5% mid-week and the 2-year sat near 4.63%. Congress's stopgap funding bill already extends federal funding through 11 December, removing near-term shutdown risk. Gold held near $4,386/oz and silver eased to $64.90/oz as the weekend's oil-driven inflation shock reinforced the case for a hike heading into Fed week. Sources: CNBC, Advisor Perspectives.

legislative.policy_html: Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — still before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue; the SBP's MPC decides on the policy rate today, with the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review mission expected in the coming weeks, widely flagged around 22-23 September.
legislative.sectors: Banks, state-owned enterprises, sovereign fund-held assets
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Investors and IMF stakeholders gain clearer governance and disclosure standards, supporting the case for the next EFF/RSF tranche. Loses: SWF-held state enterprises face tighter accountability and reporting obligations, raising near-term compliance costs.

legislative.policy_html: Oman-hosted Iran-GCC talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz were postponed indefinitely on 13 September, while Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after 10-11 September drone strikes; OPEC+'s seven core producers held October quotas unchanged near 31.01m bpd at their 6 September meeting.
legislative.sectors: Oil & gas majors, Gulf shipping/insurance, non-oil private sector
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Producers capturing higher realised prices without added supply, and Gulf non-oil sectors riding strong UAE and Saudi PMI momentum. Loses: Gulf shippers, insurers and energy importers exposed to a compounding Hormuz-and-pipeline risk premium.

legislative.policy_html: The Fed's 15-16 September FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh now carries roughly 86-90% odds of a 25bp hike per fed funds futures, after a firmer core CPI print and a fresh oil-driven inflation shock; Congress's stopgap funding bill already extends federal funding through 11 December.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Rate-sensitive value and financials if the Fed frames a hike as a one-and-done move. Loses: Growth and long-duration tech names if a hike lands alongside a persistent oil shock, reviving the risk-off tone from earlier in the week.

levels.support_note: Thursday's close, now first support; deeper support at Friday's intraday low 166,141
levels.resistance_note: Friday's intraday high; then the psychological 172,000 level

desk_stance_html: Friday's rebound was constructive on the numbers — volume rose to 687.47 million shares and breadth flipped positive (248 advancers vs 210 decliners) — but the catalyst behind it, hopes for an Iran-GCC de-escalation on Hormuz, unravelled over the weekend as Oman postponed the talks and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stayed shut. With oil gapping higher into Monday and the SBP's rate decision due today ahead of a near-coin-flip FOMC hike on 15-16 September, we'd trim broad-beta exposure into both events while retaining selective exposure to E&P and refinery-adjacent names geared to a firmer oil tape, and to non-oil GCC plays benefiting from resilient UAE and Saudi PMIs. A close back below Thursday's 168,865 pivot would reopen risk toward Friday's 166,141 low. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 rallies 1,647 points to 170,512 on Hormuz relief; oil jumps anew as Saudi pipeline stays shut and Iran-GCC talks are postponed into FOMC week

Good morning — here's the ContexAi Research desk's read on markets for Monday, 14 September 2026, covering Friday's close.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities snapped a four-day losing streak Friday: the S&P 500 rose 0.9% (+65.28 pts) to 7,656.98, the Dow gained 1.0% (+509.19 pts) to 52,573.29 and the Nasdaq added 1.0% (+251.31 pts) to 26,333.04, as August CPI (+0.4% m/m, +3.4% y/y) matched forecasts even as core inflation firmed. Fed funds futures still pushed the odds of a 25bp hike at next week's 15-16 September FOMC meeting to roughly 86-90%, up from about 70-72% a day earlier. The 10-year Treasury yield eased slightly to 4.95% after nearing 5% mid-week, while the 2-year held near 4.63%. Brent eased to $104.61/bbl and WTI to $100.05 on Friday's diplomatic hopes; gold held near $4,385.61/oz and silver fell 2.6% to $64.90/oz.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 surged 1,646.81 points (0.98%) to close at 170,511.85 on Friday, clawing back roughly half of Thursday's 3,079-point rout as reports of a planned Iran-GCC meeting on Hormuz lifted sentiment. Volume jumped to 687.47 million shares (Rs33.70bn) with 248 of 500 names advancing against 210 decliners; Meezan Bank, Fauji Fertilizer, Lucky Cement, PPL and OGDC together added 1,032 points. The State Bank's Monetary Policy Committee meets today and is widely expected to hold the policy rate at 11.5%, with August CPI at 11.15% y/y and 6-month KIBOR near 11.87%. USD/PKR interbank was steady around 277.35-277.55. The Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue ahead of the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review mission, expected around 22-23 September.

GCC
Friday's oil relief unwound fast: Oman postponed indefinitely its Monday summit between Iran and the GCC on reopening the Strait of Hormuz after Bahrain declined to attend, while Saudi Arabia's 7m-bpd East-West pipeline — the kingdom's main Hormuz bypass for roughly 5m bpd of crude — remains shut after 10-11 September drone strikes on pump stations near Riyadh and Medina. That follows Houthi strikes that wounded 73 and disrupted Saudi energy sites including the 400,000-bpd Jazan refinery. OPEC+'s seven core producers held October quotas unchanged near 31.01m bpd. Non-oil momentum held up: UAE and Saudi PMIs stood at 55.3 and 53.8 in August, both multi-month highs.

GLOBAL
US equities rebounded Friday as CPI matched forecasts, but a firmer core reading and the weekend's oil shock pushed Fed hike odds for next week's FOMC meeting to roughly 86-90%. Congress's stopgap funding bill already extends federal funding through 11 December, removing near-term shutdown risk. Oil gapped higher in early Monday trade as the Hormuz and pipeline risks compounded.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: The Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue; the SBP decides on rates today ahead of the IMF's review mission expected around 22-23 September.
• GCC: Oman postponed Iran-GCC Hormuz talks indefinitely on 13 September, while Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays shut and OPEC+ holds October quotas steady.
• Global: The Fed's 15-16 September FOMC meeting carries roughly 86-90% odds of a 25bp hike after a firmer core CPI print and a fresh oil shock, with a funding stopgap already passed through 11 December.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 — Support 168,865 (Thursday's close, now first support; deeper support at Friday's low 166,141) · Pivot 170,512 (Friday's close) · Resistance 170,765 (Friday's intraday high, then the psychological 172,000 level).

Desk stance: Friday's rebound was constructive on the numbers, but the de-escalation hopes behind it unravelled over the weekend as talks were postponed and the Saudi pipeline stayed shut. With oil gapping higher and the SBP's rate decision due today ahead of a near-coin-flip FOMC hike, we'd trim broad-beta exposure into both events while retaining selective exposure to E&P and refinery-adjacent names geared to a firmer oil tape, and to non-oil GCC plays benefiting from resilient UAE and Saudi PMIs. A close back below 168,865 would reopen risk toward Friday's 166,141 low. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
